# COMMIT after a handled error
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/transactions
#
# BigQuery documents that an exception handler may commit the transaction, but not what it keeps
# of the statements before the error, or of the statement that failed.
#
# BigQuery has answered these: the commit keeps the statements before the error and nothing of the
# statement that failed. The emulator still rejects COMMIT after a handled error, since DuckDB
# aborts the transaction on the error and has no savepoints to roll back to. The cases move to an
# end-to-end test once the emulator commits there.

CREATE TEMP TABLE committed (n INT64);
BEGIN
  BEGIN TRANSACTION;
  INSERT committed VALUES (1);
  SELECT ERROR('fail');
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM committed
?> "1"

CREATE TEMP TABLE committed (n INT64);
BEGIN
  BEGIN TRANSACTION;
  INSERT committed VALUES (1);
  INSERT committed SELECT IF(n = 3, ERROR('fail'), n) FROM UNNEST([2, 3]) AS n;
EXCEPTION WHEN ERROR THEN
  COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM committed
?> "1"
